profile.summary: DeCodon is a generative language model for protein-coding DNA that works one codon at a time. Given an NCBI Taxonomy ID for an organism, it writes new coding sequences for that organism. It is the decoder half of the cdsFM suite, released with the encoder model EnCodon, and was pretrained on coding sequences from the NCBI Genomes database.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each token is one of the 64 codons or a special token. DeCodon is loaded as a causal language model: its configuration marks it as a decoder with 12 hidden layers, 16 attention heads, hidden size 1024 and rotary position embeddings. To generate, the wrapper builds a prompt from the organism's taxonomy ID in angle brackets, so the model writes a sequence conditioned on the organism, and stops at the separator token. The same wrapper also offers embedding extraction and variant scoring.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two DeCodon checkpoints are listed: decodon-200M, the pretrained checkpoint, and decodon-200M-euk, described only as a eukaryotic expert. Hugging Face counts 157,988,032 parameters in each, fewer than the 200M in the names. This page read decodon-200M at revision 5c5c3da1 and decodon-200M-euk at revision 89ce8d5c. A result should name the checkpoint and its revision.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Decoder-only (causal) codon language model for generating coding sequences.
facts.source_locator: config.json; README: Sequence Generation with DeCodon

quotes.text: You can generate organism-specific coding sequences with DeCodon

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 12 hidden layers, 16 attention heads, hidden size 1024, intermediate size 4096, rotary position embeddings, as set in config.json of decodon-200M.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: For generation, an NCBI Taxonomy ID (the default is 9606, human), which the wrapper turns into a prompt token; a prompt can also carry starting codons. For embeddings and variant scoring, coding sequences read as codons, from a vocabulary of 64 codons and 5 special tokens.

quotes.text: The tokenizer's vocabulary consists of 64 codons and 5 special tokens

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A list of generated coding sequences as strings. The wrapper can also return sequence embeddings and variant scores.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: decodon-200M: labelled 200M in the README; Hugging Face counts 157,988,032 (F32) in the safetensors file. decodon-200M-euk: labelled 200M; Hugging Face counts 157,988,032.
facts.source_locator: README: HuggingFace table; Hugging Face API responses, safetensors

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Coding sequences from the NCBI Genomes database. The preprint abstract says the cdsFM models were pretrained on 60 million protein-coding sequences from more than 5,000 species. How the eukaryotic-expert checkpoint's data differ is not described in the sources read.

Pre-trained on 60 million protein-coding sequences from more than 5,000 species

run_guide.summary: Install the cdsFM package from GitHub and generate human coding sequences with DeCodon-200M, following the README example.
prerequisites: Python and pip. The sources do not state a Python version.
The generate method moves the model to a CUDA GPU when one is available and uses bfloat16 by default. GPU type and memory are not stated.
Code is MIT licensed. No licence is stated for the weights.

steps.title: Generate coding sequences
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from cdsFM import AutoDeCodon

# Load a pre-trained DeCodon model
model = AutoDeCodon.from_pretrained("goodarzilab/DeCodon-200M")

# Generate!
gen_seqs = model.generate(
    taxid=9606, # NCBI Taxonomy ID for Homo sapiens
    num_return_sequences=32, # Number of sequences to return
    max_length=1024, # Maximum length of the generated sequence
    batch_size=8, # Batch size for generation
)
PY
steps.explanation: The README example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads DeCodon-200M and generates 32 human coding sequences into gen_seqs.

quotes.text: taxid=9606, # NCBI Taxonomy ID for Homo sapiens
num_return_sequences=32, # Number of sequences to return

outputs: gen_seqs holds a list of generated coding sequences as strings. The snippet prints nothing.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
At commit ce6f198d the repository has no setup.py or pyproject.toml, so the pip install step may fail.
The README imports from cdsFM, but the package folder in the repository is named cdsfm (lower case). On a case-sensitive file system the import may need to be written as cdsfm.
The README loads goodarzilab/DeCodon-200M, while the wrapper's checkpoint list and Hugging Face use goodarzilab/decodon-200M.

notes: DeCodon and EnCodon (folder 22-encodon) come from the same repository and preprint. The existing source gfm-guides-20261014-evo2-brixi2026-source-supplementary-information is the Evo 2 supplement, which evaluated DeCodon; it was not read.
